claims.text: A tailored graded interfacial layer produced using controlled surface texturing and annealing will significantly enhance adhesion between a Cu substrate and an HEA coating.
The proposed interfacial treatment will preserve the HEA coating's superior wear resistance.
Surface texturing followed by controlled annealing before HEA deposition can create a thin, graded interfacial layer on Cu.
The resulting interface will have nano-to-microscale texturing and a chemical composition gradient.
The graded interface will bridge compositional differences between Cu and the HEA.
The graded interface will bridge thermal-expansion differences between Cu and the HEA.
Chemical inertness at the Cu–HEA interface inherently limits bonding.
A thermal-expansion mismatch exists between Cu and the unspecified HEA.
The graded layer minimizes chemical inertness and thermal-expansion mismatch at the Cu–HEA interface.
Minimizing interfacial incompatibility improves stress distribution and bonding at the interface.
The treatment will produce a substantial improvement in adhesion strength relative to direct deposition on untreated Cu.
The treated coating system will retain or enhance its wear resistance.
Direct deposition of an HEA coating on untreated Cu typically produces poor adhesion.
Poor adhesion on untreated Cu is caused by interfacial incompatibility.
The interfacial treatment may be less effective under extreme thermal cycling or mechanical stress above moderate levels.
Under extreme conditions, the gradient layer may not compensate fully for large thermal-expansion differences.
